identity.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks: Mechanistic Evidence from Attention Head Specialization in Large Language Models

problem.claim: Explain how jailbreak attacks bypass safety alignment in large language models.

gap.claim: The mechanisms underlying jailbreak attacks remain poorly understood.

contributions.claim: Identifies early-layer Adversarially Compromised Heads (ACHs), which attacks suppress, and mid-layer Safety-Aligned Heads (SAHs), whose activations remain robust.
Uses ablations and token-level attribution to characterize the roles and attack-template dependence of ACH suppression and SAH activity.
Shows that reading persistent safety activations without training can provide aggregate detection performance with adversarial robustness.

stated_novelty.claim: Terms the persistence of internal safety signals alongside attack-suppressed harmful-feature pathways “Robust Harmful Features.”

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that suppressing a small number of ACHs induces jailbreak-like behavior on inputs normally refused, while removing SAHs substantially weakens mid-layer safety activations.
The authors report that ACH suppression is specifically driven by attack-template tokens.
The authors report competitive aggregate detection performance and strong adversarial robustness from simply reading persistent activations, without training.

narrative_sequence.summary: Jailbreak mechanisms are described as poorly understood.
Attacks are reported to selectively suppress specific attention heads rather than eliminate safety features comprehensively.
ACHs are associated with early-layer suppression, whereas mid-layer SAHs retain robust activations during successful attacks.
Ablations support differentiated ACH and SAH roles, and attribution links ACH suppression to attack-template tokens.
Reading persistent activations without training is reported to yield competitive detection with adversarial robustness.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a named mechanistic phenomenon with differentiated components, intervention evidence, token-level attribution, and a practical readout.

lessons.interpretation: A compact mechanism claim becomes more informative when structural, intervention-based, explanatory, and application-level evidence are connected.
lessons.application: For a mechanistic paper, define component roles first, then pair each role with an intervention and an interpretable signal before presenting downstream utility.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the study has no meaningful internal decomposition or when interventions cannot distinguish competing explanations.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide model identities, datasets, sample sizes, quantitative detection metrics, or baseline definitions for “competitive” performance.
The reported causal support and robustness conditions cannot be assessed beyond the abstract-level descriptions.
